title: P7: the transform is linear over the base
statement:
Let $V_0\to S_0$ be the rank-$r$ vector bundle of [def-fd-kernel], let
$p:V\to S$ and $p':V^\vee\to S$ be the structure morphisms, and let
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ be the transform of [def-fd-transform]. For
$K\in D^b_c(V,E)$ and $N\in D^b_c(S,E)$ there is an isomorphism, natural
in $K$ and $N$,

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(K\otimes^L_Ep^*N\bigr)\cong
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\otimes^L_E{p'}^*N .
$$

In particular:

1. for $N$ from the base,
   $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(p^*N)\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\underline{E})\otimes^L_E{p'}^*N$,
   so the transform of a base-changed sheaf is the base change of the
   transform of the unit;
2. (*Tate twists*) for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K$,
   $$
   \operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl(K(m)\bigr)\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)(m),
   $$
   with the Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist]; if $K$ carries a Weil
   structure, this isomorphism is one of Weil complexes.

proof.text: Use the adic coefficient setting of [def-fourier-set], in particular the standing convention that the values of $\psi$ lie in $E$. All tensor products below are the completed integral tensor followed by rationalization, as specified by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The schemes $S,V,V^\vee,W:=V\times_SV^\vee$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. On integral representatives the natural comparison of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] identifies this tensor with the ordinary derived tensor over the completed coefficient sheaf. Thus the associators, symmetry and unit constraints of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], applied on small representatives of the pro-etale sites, give those same constraints for the tensor used here: conjugate each constraint by the natural tensor-completion comparison. On morphisms rationalize these constraints using the formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. They are natural isomorphisms; their equations remain equations after rationalization.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1-2: coefficient interpretation and tensor constraints; Stacks Tag 0FPT, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived; Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.5.5

proof.text: Let $p_1:W\to V$ and $p_2:W\to V^\vee$ be the projections of [def-fd-kernel], and put $\pi=pp_1=p'p_2$. The vector-bundle map $p$ is affine of finite type: over a trivializing affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ its coordinate algebra is $A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. It is separated, since its affine-chart diagonal is the closed immersion defined by the surjection $A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\otimes_A A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\to A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. Apply [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] to $p$ and $p'$ to see that its base change $p_2$ is separated of finite type. The argument also applies when $r=0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: the geometric hypothesis on the second projection

proof.text:
The monoidal pullback isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the pullback-composition isomorphisms of [sk-thm-sf-compatibility] (1), used with $pp_1=p'p_2$, give the following composite, natural in both inputs:
$$p_1^*(K\otimes_E^Lp^*N)\simeq p_1^*K\otimes_E^Lp_1^*p^*N\simeq p_1^*K\otimes_E^L\pi^*N\simeq p_1^*K\otimes_E^Lp_2^*{p'}^*N.$$
These are the completed/rational pullbacks in the cited statements; no discrete non-torsion etale comparison is used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: the three pullback identifications; Stacks Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, at finite level and its stated coefficient transports

proof.text:
Set $A=p_1^*K\otimes_E^L\mathcal K_\psi$ and $L={p'}^*N$. The integrand assertion in [def-fd-kernel] places $A$ in $D^b_c(W,E)$. Apply [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] to integral representatives and rationalize by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; this places $L$ in $D^b_c(V^\vee,E)$, and [lem-weil-field-tor-amplitude], with coefficient field $E$, gives its finite Tor amplitude. Tensor the isomorphism of step 3 with $\mathcal K_\psi$, and apply the associativity and symmetry constraints from step 1, moving $p_2^*L$ past the kernel. This gives
$$p_1^*(K\otimes_E^Lp^*N)\otimes_E^L\mathcal K_\psi\simeq A\otimes_E^Lp_2^*L.$$
The same preservation statement and its rationalization show that both sides lie in the specified bounded constructible category.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2-3: rearrange the integrand and check the coefficient domains

proof.text:
Apply clause (5) of [prop-functor-package] to $f=p_2$, first input $A$, and second input $L$. Step 2 verifies separated finite type, and step 4 verifies exactly the constructibility and finite-Tor hypotheses. The inverse of its projection isomorphism, composed with $p_{2,!}$ of the preceding integrand isomorphism, is
$$p_{2,!}\bigl(p_1^*(K\otimes_E^Lp^*N)\otimes_E^L\mathcal K_\psi\bigr)\simeq p_{2,!}(A)\otimes_E^LL.$$
It is natural in $K,N$: the projection map is natural in its two arguments by [prop-sf-pf-coherence], and all previous maps are natural.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: compact-support projection formula, with the isomorphism read in the inverse direction

proof.text:
Shift the last isomorphism by $[r]$. The integral right-shift comparison of [lem-sf-completed-tensor-shift-right], followed by rationalization as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], gives $L\otimes_E^L X[r]\simeq(L\otimes_E^LX)[r]$. With the symmetry of step 1 this gives
$$X[r]\otimes_E^LL\simeq L\otimes_E^LX[r]\simeq(L\otimes_E^LX)[r]\simeq(X\otimes_E^LL)[r].$$
Use its inverse for $X=p_{2,!}(A)$ and the definition [def-fd-transform]. The result is
$$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K\otimes_E^Lp^*N)\simeq\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\otimes_E^L{p'}^*N.$$
The shift comparison and symmetry are natural, so this establishes the asserted bifunctorial isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: commute the normalization shift with tensor

proof.text: The coefficient unit $E_V$ is bounded constructible by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Specialize step 6 to $K=E_V$, and apply the left unit constraint from step 1, $E_V\otimes_E^Lp^*N\simeq p^*N$. This proves clause (1), naturally in $N$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 5: specialization to the coefficient unit

proof.text: For $m\in\mathbf Z$ take $N=E_S(m)$. This is a bounded constructible invertible coefficient line by [prop-weil-twist-preserves]; its negative powers are included in that statement. The canonical Tate pullback comparisons of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] give $p^*E_S(m)\simeq E_V(m)$ and ${p'}^*E_S(m)\simeq E_{V^\vee}(m)$. Apply step 6 to this $N$ and use the definition $K(m)=K\otimes_E^LE_V(m)$ from [def-wf-tate-twist]. This proves clause (2) on the underlying complexes for all integers $m$, including $m=0$ and $m<0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 6: Tate twists pulled back from the base, using the existing all-integer pullback theorem

proof.text: Suppose $K$ has a Weil structure. The maps $p,p',p_1,p_2$ and the kernel in [def-fd-kernel] are defined over $k_0$. By [lem-fix-weil-operations], their pullback, tensor and compact-support images carry the canonical Weil structures, and the composition, exchange and projection maps used above are equivariant. The Tate lines have their prescribed roots-of-unity Frobenius structure [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. The Tate pullback comparisons commute with this structure: for each finite roots-of-unity sheaf, pulling a section along the structural map and along Frobenius in either order gives the same section, since the corresponding scheme square commutes. This equality respects the power transition maps, tensor powers and the evaluation maps defining negative powers; it therefore holds for the canonical all-integer comparisons of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]. Tensor constraints are constraints of the induced Weil tensor operation. Shifting a commuting square shifts both of its sides, so the shift comparisons also preserve it. Consequently the composite $e_K$ of step 8 satisfies $e_K\varphi_{\operatorname{FT}(K(m))}=\varphi_{\operatorname{FT}(K)(m)}\Phi_{V^\vee}^*(e_K)$, exactly the morphism condition in [def-wf-weil-category]. Its inverse satisfies the same equation by composing with inverses. Thus the isomorphism is one of Weil complexes.

source.place: Proof paragraph 6, final sentence: the Frobenius square for the actual composite
